text:
$BABA $ABNB $DASH - TRUMP ADMINISTRATION WEIGHS DISCLOSURE RULES FOR CHINESE AI USE

The Trump administration is considering requiring U.S. companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models, Reuters reports.

The proposal, discussed by the Treasury Department and White House, could affect companies such as Airbnb, which uses Alibaba's Qwen for customer service.

Rather than imposing outright restrictions, officials are exploring transparency requirements to discourage reliance on Chinese technology.

No formal rule has been announced.

The move reflects growing Washington scrutiny of DeepSeek, Qwen and Kimi as Chinese AI adoption expands.

text:
$NVDA 最新Q3财报财务数据和下一季预测全面超预期，粉碎的是空头的“半导体算力周期见顶和估值塌陷”的小作文陷阱。  

一个人能活成黄仁勋这种离职能带崩2万亿自己创业公司市值，还能带崩整个AI泡沫，那真是可以笑傲江湖了。如何真正的解读背后事件以及财报中关键的英伟达投资策略“范式”转移？

真正的行业专家背景买方投资看的当然不只是一个收入和毛利超预期，这都是大概率。要看到这种英伟达顶级的技术路线和工程实现能力，这才是真正的护城河

8月启动发售新一代Rubin第一个季度就200亿订单确认，部署效率1个月比上一代快一倍，而且新一代的token/瓦的效率是上一代Blackwell的十倍提升，意味着1GW的Rubin收入就是一年4-500亿。

这不是简单卖GPU，而是真正的系统工程，自己的CPU/连接/安全芯片/明年上光互连CPO量产又一能效提升。加上模块化工厂，按上接点就挣钱。这个背景就是大的行业需求暴涨，特别是Agentic AI对于算力需求，哪怕老卡早期前2代的租金都在大涨。

收入多元化除了云大厂占1半，这也是为什么英伟达要扶持第三方新云公司，包括企业/主权等收入，降低依赖于单一大客户风险，何况中国收入为0，目前北美/欧日等需求直接填补空档，供不应求。

哪怕是市场担心的表外担保生态融资，来虚增收入，完全可以证伪。6400亿表外承诺，近4000亿是供应链采购承诺主要是锁定上游晶圆/HBM存储和封装产能，这是必须的，因为英伟达自己是轻资产，对于上游的供应链掌控重要性。当然老黄不在有短期影响，但对于英伟达这种体量客户，靠个人关系已经不是长久之计，必然规范大势所趋，这方面何况作为最大的客户，英伟达是甲方，不担心台湾供应链不保障的风险

另外1000亿是自用云服务；真正新云neocloud保底租赁也就是320亿，而且都是有明确前置条件，就是全部上线才担保，现在供不应求之下，风险何在？另外1000多亿是OpenAI的20年独家租约，至少目前看不到证伪。

目前市场大跌因为黄仁勋的时代落幕，当然作为创始人的远见和个人魄力是有折价，这主要体现在可能未来3-5年战略的选择，但是对于AI时代真正的王者和领头羊，老黄一人独裁的邪修管理风格，也是必然在企业进入系统化竞争的平台后，管理范式的转移，向“开宗立派”转移，只不过，他个人事件离职，加速了这个转移而已。

从投资策略和估值角度，事件性冲击短期当然是重点，根据不同的事件会有好的买入时点，结合合理的估值，因为基本面虽然强，但是整体的估值溢价需要下调到一个中长期合理的区间，同时也要考虑本质性，一些竞争力丧失的风险，比如法律和治理风险，人才流失风险。

颗粒度更细的投资策略和估值，见订阅者专享。教育分享。

• Samsung Electro-Mechanics: Expanding substrate production capabilities at existing factories in South Korea.

• Amkor: Nearly $3B in previously announced agreements supporting advanced chip packaging expansion in Arizona and South Korea.

• SPIL: Multibillion-dollar funding from Nvidia to expand advanced packaging capacity in Taiwan, with additional capacity expected by mid-2029.

• Foxconn: Using its global manufacturing network to support production of next-generation GPUs and networking systems.

Nvidia also confirmed that Vera Rubin NVL72 and Vera CPUs began volume shipments in fiscal Q3, using TSMC’s 5nm, 3nm and CoWoS advanced packaging technologies.

Powell’s November 17, 2026 earnings call supports continued strength in electrical equipment, power-generation infrastructure, LNG equipment and specialized construction. The most important signal is not simply expanding demand: manufacturing capacity is translating into revenue while underlying margins remain resilient. However, the call also exposes significant differences in economic quality across the investment chain. Standardized data-center equipment carries greater scope-change risk than traditional engineered industrial projects, skilled labor is becoming a more important execution constraint, and exceptionally strong equipment-manufacturer cash flow should not be extrapolated to installation contractors. The strongest positive implications concern earnings durability through 2027 and 2028; the strongest negative implications concern the permanence of scarcity-driven pricing, fixed-price execution economics and working-capital requirements. Most relevant peers had already reported their September-quarter results, making Powell’s disclosures incremental corroboration rather than an advance signal of those completed quarters. text:
$NVDA $TSM TSMC AND NVIDIA: THE DIVISION OF LABOR AFTER THE JENSEN TRANSITION

The most critical operational learning from NVIDIA's Q3 FY27 earnings call on 11/17/26 was not a number. It was a name: TSMC.

THE TELL FROM THE CALL

Answering Vivek Arya's question on what stays durable through the leadership transition, interim CEO Colette Kress said: "I see right now the leadership, even from TSMC, that was in our offices just this week, also fully engaged in helping us. We secured memory. We secured advanced packaging."

The sentence was not in prepared remarks. It was offered, in a governance answer, as evidence that the company's moat survives the founder's exit. Of every institution Kress could have named, she named the foundry, and she named it at the level of "leadership in our offices this week," meaning the engagement is executive to executive during the transition week itself, not a standing purchase order.

The same day, NVIDIA published its supply-chain release, "NVIDIA Expands Commitments With Supply Chain Partners to Support AI Infrastructure Buildout." In it, TSMC SVP and deputy co-COO Dr. Kevin Zhang is quoted: "TSMC and NVIDIA share a longstanding partnership built on semiconductor innovation. This deep collaboration allows us to plan for future technology requirements and prepare our manufacturing capabilities as NVIDIA brings new platforms to market." The release states that Vera Rubin NVL72 and Vera CPUs began volume shipments in Q3 FY27 leveraging TSMC's 5nm

text:
$NVDA earnings transcript + industry read through. To sum it up: "Demand far exceeds supply".  

- Good news for the $MU / Samsung memory longs: 

"Our supply commitments increased from $279B last quarter to $390B, primarily related to the multi-year procurement of memory supply". (from SEC filings, not call)

This is a a major leap Q/Q in supply procurement.  

- "We expect revenue to grow approximately 75% year-over-year, up from 70%." (upward revision, likely due to capacity constraints easing)

(new agreements with Kinsus and Samsung Electro-Mechanics support additional ABF substrate capacity)

- NVIDIA said industry cloud backlog increased from $2 trillion to $2.5 trillion in a single quarter. While GPU rental pricing is continuing to rise dramatically:

Hopper GPUs: 2x their original pricing
B300 GPUs: +60% since introduction
Utilization: NVIDIA says its own compute is fully utilized across the hyperscalers and neoclouds it serves.

- "Our co-packaged optics roadmap remains on track"

Optical networking keeps growing rapidly ($21B+ in quarterly networking), CPO scale out switches has entered volume production. With Lambda earlier announcing production deployment of Nvidia photonics CPO switches. 

- "Under these agreements, we will earn revenue on the upfront sale of our infrastructure" So there's additional recurring economics coming from Neoclouds. 

But just points to industry acceleration from memory to CPO to neoclouds, relative to markets pricing in collapse.

text:
I'll leave it up to your judgement. From my point of view, there's $956M in commitments vs. $605M cash so they needed more financing for their buildout. 

However two things stood out:

1. Management commentary around financing: CFO said US bank financing could reach $500m, and that profits would help fund operations. CFO said share price mattered and that they'd lean more into debt. 

So their actions went contrary to management commentary. 

If you look at $COHR, they fund capacity expansion from upfront prepayments. There's other ways to do it too like convertible notes.

2. Capital allocation issue: they spent $102M on three Texas buildings they had under lease. Which was around $5M annualized and I'm sure they're aware market financing conditions are tight. 

2 weeks after buying buildings when they were already relatively low on cash... AOI decided to do yet another $550M ATM. 

It's just a bit hard to justify.

Jensen Left. Nvidia’s Role as the Central Bank of AI Didn’t.

en_summary: $NVDA's future commitments climbed to $518B, from $366B last quarter. Separately, Nvidia disclosed
text:
$NVDA's future commitments climbed to $518B, from $366B last quarter.

Separately, Nvidia disclosed $32B in conditional neocloud agreements, down from $36B.

Here's the breakdown of the $518B:
> Supply and capacity: $390B (vs. $279B), largely multi-year memory purchases
> Cloud services & data center leases: $102B (vs. $54B)
> Equity investments: $20B (vs. $25B)
> Capital expenditures: $6B (vs. $8B)

The additional $32B in neocloud commitments only takes effect if partners secure financing and the compute capacity is deployed, operational, and accepted by Nvidia.
